Four things found while auditing that are not verdicts on my items but belong in the record.

(a) NEW DEFECT INTRODUCED BY THE P8 DOCUMENTATION COMMIT. wooldid.sthlp:613-614, added by 81c284b (verified: `git log -S "a handful of draws is a legitimate smoke test"` returns only that commit), reads "Raising the draw count is the only fix; neither engine has a hard minimum, since a handful of draws is a legitimate smoke test." That is false and contradicts both the code and the help: ado:5657-5658 refuses `permreps()` below 20 ("Error: permreps() must be at least 20: the engine refuses inference on fewer than 20 completed replications..."), sthlp:453 says "{cmd:permreps()} must be at least 20", and review_process/research_2026-09-08/engine_parity.md lists the asymmetry as a keep-and-document item ("permreps() has a hard floor and reps() correctly has only a caution"). The sentence is in the P7 disposition's own p-value map, so it undercuts the section it was written to support.

(b) NEW DEFECT INTRODUCED BY P7 ACCIDENT 2. wooldid.sthlp:674, the saveplots() entry, still says the plot-data file is engine-only: "and, under {cmd:bootstrap()} or {cmd:permute()} with {it:makecfxplots}, one {it:name}{cmd:_cfx.dta} holding every plotted continuous-treatment point." Since commit 20c0ec9 the analytic path writes it too (ado:4204, 506-517), pinned by test_cfxlat L6. The behaviour ruling is carried out; the help was not updated to match, so the one place a user would look now understates the artifact.

(c) The accident-3 residual, restated because it is the drift the ruling existed to stop: sthlp:509's bootstrap incompatibility list carries no reasons and sthlp:455's permute list omits multi-way cluster() and customvce(). The new table at sthlp:1193-1215 is correct and complete against the ado gates, so the two inline lists are now the only surface that can drift away from it.

(d) The one undocumented engine difference I found while sampling the disposition: the failed-replication asymmetry (CS-32, CS-45). permute's policy is stated at sthlp:452; the bootstrap's caution-on-any-failure and refusal-only-at-zero policy is nowhere in the help, and no enginediff paragraph or table row explains why the reactions differ. This is the difference whose verdict the errata ruling reversed, so it is the one a reader is most likely to look up.
